extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, USPTO examiners, patent attorneys, agents, and inventors
extracted.subtask_description: Authoritative statutory provisions from Title 35 U.S.C. (selected sections) that set forth requirements, conditions, procedures, and remedies for patentability, prosecution, post-grant challenges, and enforcement in the United States. Useful as the legal rubric for drafting, prosecuting, examining, and litigating patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions patentable (35 U.S.C. §101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory foundation for patentable subject matter; establishes that certain inventions or discoveries are eligible for patent protection (see §101 for statutory language and judicial interpretation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for patentability; novelty (35 U.S.C. §102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions for patentability; novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that claimed subject matter must be novel (not anticipated by prior art). Related provisions address bars to patenting such as printed publication, public use, sale, and other statutory bars (see index references to printed publication bar and public use or sale).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for patentability; non-obvious subject matter (35 U.S.C. §103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions for patentability; non-obvious subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires that claimed inventions not be obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art based on the prior art; central statutory test for inventive step (obviousness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (35 U.S.C. §100 and related notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions relevant to patent law are set out (see §100 and pre-/post-AIA notes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory definitions (e.g., 'patentee', 'United States' as used in Title 35) frame interpretation of substantive and procedural provisions throughout Title 35.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification requirements (35 U.S.C. §112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory requirements for the specification (written description, enablement, best mode (where applicable), and definiteness of claims); governs sufficiency of disclosure and claim clarity; referenced as 'Contents of specification' in index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims (statutory and indexing references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are an essential part of the patent and define the scope of the invention (index references: 'Claim').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must satisfy statutory requirements (patentability, clarity, supported by specification). Reissue and reexamination rules interact with claim scope (e.g., reissue for defective claims, no new matter on reissue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings and models; specimens (35 U.S.C. §§113–114)
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings; models, specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When necessary, drawings must be provided and specimens/models may be required; requirements affect sufficiency of disclosure and examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or declaration and related formalities (35 U.S.C. §115 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventor's oath or declaration; oath/declaration requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application must include an oath or declaration by the inventor (or a declaration in lieu of oath where allowed); statutory provisions address requirements, persons who may sign if inventor is deceased or incapacitated, and consequences of defective execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship and joint inventors (35 U.S.C. §116 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors; joint inventors; requirements concerning inventorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines who qualifies as an inventor, rules for joint inventors, and procedures to correct inventorship; interplay with assignment and ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date, filing requirements and application definitions (35 U.S.C. §21; §111)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing date and day for taking action; Application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes what constitutes a filing date and the formal requirements for applications (including pre-AIA and post-AIA distinctions, provisional applications, and types of applications), which affect priority, patent term, and prior art status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit of earlier filing date; right of priority (35 U.S.C. §§119–121, 365)
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefit of earlier filing date; right of priority; right of priority under treaties and international filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for claiming benefit of earlier U.S. filings or foreign priority under treaty provisions and PCT; affects effective filing date for novelty and obviousness determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential status of applications; publication of patent applications (35 U.S.C. §122)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential status of applications; publication of patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines when and how applications are published, and what remains confidential; includes provisions limiting pre-issuance opposition in certain circumstances (see index reference to pre-issuance opposition prohibition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of application; notice of rejection; prosecution timing (35 U.S.C. §§131–133)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination of application; notice of rejection; time for prosecuting application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the Office's examination responsibilities, requirement to notify applicant of rejections with reasons, and statutory time limits for applicant responses and prosecution steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and review of examiner decisions (35 U.S.C. §§134, 141 and PTAB provisions §6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board and to the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit; proceedings on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes administrative appeal routes from examiner decisions to the PTAB and judicial appeals to the Federal Circuit, including procedural requirements and rights to rehearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation proceedings and interferences (35 U.S.C. §135 and pre-AIA interference provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Derivation proceedings; (pre-AIA) interferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures to resolve disputes over who first invented or who derived claimed subject matter; derivation replaced interference post-AIA, with specific procedural rules in the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant procedures: reexamination, inter partes review, post-grant review (Chapters 30–32; §§301–329, 311–329)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation of prior art and written statements; requests for reexamination; inter partes review; post-grant review; petitions and institution standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory framework for challenging issued patents at the Office (ex parte reexamination, inter partes review, post-grant review), including petition requirements, institution, relation to other proceedings, settlement, and Board decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue of defective patents (35 U.S.C. §251–253)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue of defective patents; disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows correction of defective patents (e.g., defective claims) via reissue subject to statutory limits (no new matter; effect on term; intervening rights). Also includes disclaimer provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term, term adjustment and term extension (35 U.S.C. §§154, 156)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contents and term of patent; provisional rights; extension of patent term; term adjustment for administrative delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies patent term, mechanisms for patent term adjustment or extension (e.g., for administrative delays, regulatory review, secrecy orders, derivation proceedings, appellate review), and provisional rights; affects enforceable term and remedies timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy of certain inventions and foreign filing rules (35 U.S.C. §§181–188, §184)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secrecy of certain inventions and withholding of patent; abandonment for unauthorized disclosure; filing of application in foreign country; right to compensation for secrecy orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government-imposed secrecy orders can withhold patents for national security reasons; statutes govern unauthorized disclosure, compensation, and rules for foreign filings when secrecy applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent rights in inventions made with federal assistance (35 U.S.C. §§200–212)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy and objective; disposition of rights; march-in rights; domestic and foreign protection of federally owned inventions; relation to antitrust laws and licensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets requirements and rights for inventions arising from federally funded research (e.g., Bayh-Dole-type provisions), including disposition of rights, march-in, and licensing constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership, assignment, and joint ownership (35 U.S.C. §§261–262)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership; assignment; joint owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory rules for recordation of assignments, rights of assignees, treatment of joint owners, and related procedures for ownership changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and enforcement for infringement (35 U.S.C. §§281–289)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedy for infringement of patent; presumption of validity; injunction; damages; attorney fees; limitation on damages; marking and notice provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines available remedies (injunctions, damages, enhanced damages, attorney fees), presumption of patent validity and defenses, statute of limitations on damages, and notice/marking rules (including requirements for provisional rights and marking-related limits on damages).

rubrics_metrics.name: False marking (35 U.S.C. §292)
rubrics_metrics.description: False marking and penalties for falsely marking an article as patented or patent pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides causes of action and penalties for deceptive marking of products (including 'patent pending' misuse), with specified statutory consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art citations to the Office and ex parte reexamination (35 U.S.C. Chapter 30, §301 et seq.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art citations to Office and ex parte reexamination of patents; procedures for submitting prior art and requesting reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanisms for third parties or the Office to submit prior art and request reexamination of patents; includes certificate issuance for patentability/unpatentability and claim cancellation outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes review applicability and petitions (35 U.S.C. §311 and following)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes review; petitions; institution; conduct; settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines scope and procedures for inter partes review (IPR), petition content and institution standards, relation to other proceedings, and Board decision process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant patents (35 U.S.C. §§161–164)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents for plants; description and claim requirements; grant; assistance of Department of Agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special statutory provisions for plant patents including required description, claim form, fees, and cooperation with agricultural agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patents and international design applications (35 U.S.C. §§171–173; Hague Agreement chapters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents for designs; right of priority; term of design patent; international design application procedures under the Hague Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets requirements and term for design patents and procedures for international design filings (definition, filing date, right of priority, examination, relief from prescribed time limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules governing practitioners and representation before the Office (35 U.S.C. §2(b)(2)(D); §33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations may govern recognition and conduct of agents, attorneys, or other persons representing applicants; prohibition on unauthorized practice and requirement to show good moral character and qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require practitioners to demonstrate qualifications and moral character; unauthorized representation is prohibited and subject to sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees, funding, small and micro entity status (35 U.S.C. §§41–42; §123)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent fees; Patent and Trademark Office funding; definitions and eligibility for small entity and micro entity fee reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory fee schedules, Office funding provisions, and reduced fee structures for small and micro entities; the Office must recognize public interest in broad access via reduced fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates of correction and correction of inventorship (35 U.S.C. §§254–256)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificate of correction of Patent and Trademark Office mistake; certificate of correction of applicant's mistake; correction of named inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures to correct errors in issued patents (clerical or applicant mistakes) and to correct named inventors; statutory remedies and procedures specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional applications and provisional rights (references §111(b), §119(e), §154)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional applications; effect on filing date and provisional rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional application filings can establish priority and may afford provisional rights under specified conditions; statutory cross-references set the interplay with non-provisional filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival and reinstatement (index references §27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revival of applications; reinstatement of reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory mechanisms to revive applications or reinstate proceedings where certain delays were unintentional or other statutory criteria are met; affects prosecution continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of practice, testimony, subpoenas and evidentiary procedures (35 U.S.C. §§23–26 and §2 rulemaking authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for taking testimony; subpoenas to witnesses; declarations in lieu of oath; effect of defective execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director authorized to adopt rules of practice governing procedures for testimony, subpoena power, and formalities affecting evidence and procedural compliance in Office proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent marking, notice, and limitations on damages (35 U.S.C. §287 and related indexing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitation on damages and other remedies; marking and notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory marking and notice rules affect the patentee's ability to recover damages for infringement; proper marking and notice are prerequisites for certain damage periods.
